_comment: DEMO, not the default: odometry that is wrong the way real odometry is wrong.
The odometry integrator used to receive the *true* chassis geometry, so the commonest real
error -- a wheel radius that is not what the drawing says -- could not be expressed at all.
It now builds its own geometry from odom.geometry (sensors.odom_geometry).
Run it in the window and drive a straight line: the odometry ghost (`o`) pulls ahead of the
robot by 5 cm per metre -- measured 0.61 m of 'odom off' after 12 m of lane, with the truth
still on its line:
./lab sim --world track --config config/demo_odom_error.json
Watch it from the outside (the ghost of the reference solution, no keyboard needed):
./lab run --world production --config config/demo_odom_error.json \
--robot muster --controller student/solution.py --seconds 30
See what it does to the graded tasks (measured with the reference solution, seed 1):
./lab grade --config config/demo_odom_error.json --task alle --controller student/solution.py
T1 ok, T2 ok (closure 0.18 m on a 4 m square -- the controller corrects its own drift),
T3 FAILS with 26 wall contacts: the LIDAR task navigates by odometry between the walls,
and a robot that believes it drove 8 % further than it did comes out in a wall,
T4 ok (0.17 m): the GPS approach does not trust the wheel odometry.
Why a file and not the default: the thresholds in config/tasks.json are calibrated on correct
wheel constants, and model error is not a noise knob -- it scales with the distance driven,
so every measurement taken over odometry (T2 closure, T3 target, the odometry feed of every
Kalman filter in experiment 2) shifts with it. Do not grade with this file unless you also
recalibrate.
What each term of odom.geometry does (defaults: 1, 1, 1, 1, [0,0]; see mecanum_lab/types.py):
wheel_radius_scale 1.05   every wheel speed converts to 5 % more distance, so the path
scales -- and so does the yaw rate, because the same radius sits
in the turn equation. On its own: 12 m driven, 12.6 m reported.
lever_scale 0.97          the assumed lever arm a = lx+ly is 3 % short, so the turn rate
comes out 3 % too big: a commanded revolution ends rotated. On
its own 11 deg after 360 deg; together with the 1.05 radius here
the two add up to 8.25 % and measured 28 deg after one round.
wheel_base_scale          only the vehicle length mis-measured (lx): vx, vy and omega mix
in the wrong ratio while the speed stays about right.
scale_xy                  body velocity too fast/slow while the yaw rate stays right --
wrong radius but honest gyro: a commanded circle becomes a spiral.
bias_xy [0,0]             constant offset of the reported pose: the odom origin is not where
you think it is. A shifted world, not drift.
_comment_tail: 1.05 radius + 0.97 lever is what two worn wheels and a reprinted hub add up to.
